5 تسقّى It (a thing) received, or admitted, moisture, (M, TA,) or irrigation; or became plentifully irrigated, or succulent, or sappy. (M, K, TA.) The Hudhalee (El-Mutanakhkhil, TA) says. “مُجَدَّلٌ يَتَسَقَّى جِلْدُهُ دَمَهُ
كَمَا تَقَطَّرَ جِذْعُ الدَّوْمَةِ القُطُلُ
” meaning [Thrown down upon the ground, his skin] becomes drenched with his blood (يَتَشَرَّبُهُ) [like as drips the severed trunk of the Theban palm-tree]: or, as some relate the verse, يَتَكَسَّى [becomes overspread, here meaning suffused], from الكِسْوَةُ. (S, TA.) ―
-b2- تَسَقَّتِ الإِبِلُ الحَوْذَانَ (assumed tropical:) The camels ate the حوذان (a certain plant, TA) in its fresh and moist state, and became fat upon it. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
